Statement: Within the reviewed literature corpus, there is limited evidence of an integrated resource-aware smartphone visual-inspection system in which device-state-driven runtime adaptation is coupled with confidence-aware downstream verification, particularly for recovering inspection performance under resource-induced model/configuration degradation.
Evaluation_Method: Literature boundary (Steps 9.7-9.9C); experiments E1;E2;E3

Statement: Can confidence-aware downstream verification recover inspection accuracy lost when a resource-constrained smartphone dynamically downgrades its inference configuration under changing device conditions?
Independent_Variables: baseline condition;resource-pressure condition (R0-R3, measured telemetry logged as manipulation check);inference configuration;adaptation state;confidence threshold
Evaluation_Method: Decision rule over H1, H2, H5 (hypotheses.md section 7); E2;E3
Falsification_Condition: H1 not supported (not testable) or F2 or F3 holds

Statement: How does resource-driven runtime adaptation change defect-detection performance and resource consumption on a resource-constrained smartphone, relative to the static configurations it switches between?
Independent_Variables: resource-pressure condition (R0-R3, measured telemetry logged as manipulation check);inference configuration;adaptation state
Evaluation_Method: E1 forced sweep; E2 B3 vs B1 and B2

Statement: What proportion of the inspection-performance loss caused by resource-driven configuration downgrading does confidence-aware verification recover, and how does that proportion vary with resource state and verification action?
Evaluation_Method: E2 B5 vs B3; E3 B5 vs B5-F

Statement: How do confidence distributions and calibration differ across inference configurations, and do they differ across resource states when the configuration is held fixed?
Evaluation_Method: E1 forced sweep

Statement: What latency, energy, thermal, memory and verification-action overhead does confidence-aware verification add, per inspected item and per verified item?
Evaluation_Method: E1; E2 B5 vs B3 and B4 vs fixed configuration
Falsification_Condition: H3 falsified (no overhead beyond measurement resolution); F4

Statement: Does combining resource adaptation with confidence verification give a more favourable accuracy-efficiency trade-off than either mechanism alone, and how does it compare with the static best and static lightweight configurations?
Evaluation_Method: E2 Pareto and matched-budget comparison of B1-B5

Statement: Design a resource-aware runtime inference policy for smartphone visual inspection.
Independent_Variables: resource-pressure condition (R0-R3, measured telemetry logged as manipulation check);adaptation state
Evaluation_Method: Policy specification in configs/; behaviour logged in E2

Statement: Quantify inspection-performance degradation under controlled resource pressure and configuration downgrading.
Independent_Variables: resource-pressure condition (R0-R3, measured telemetry logged as manipulation check);inference configuration
Evaluation_Method: E1; E2 B3 vs B1

Statement: Design a confidence-aware downstream verification mechanism.
Evaluation_Method: Verification-policy specification in configs/; E3 distinguishes it from a fixed threshold

Statement: Measure how much performance degradation the verification mechanism recovers.
Evaluation_Method: E2 B5 vs B3

Statement: Characterize confidence/calibration changes across configurations and resource states.
Evaluation_Method: E1

Statement: Quantify latency, energy, thermal, memory, and verification overhead.
Evaluation_Method: E1; E2

Statement: Compare the combined strategy against appropriate ablation baselines.
Evaluation_Method: E2 B1-B5; E3 B5-F

Statement: Determine whether the combined approach produces a statistically and practically meaningful accuracy-efficiency improvement.
Evaluation_Method: Pre-registered tests with Holm correction and SESOI equivalence bounds

Statement: Resource-driven runtime downgrading decreases inspection performance relative to the best static configuration under equivalent task conditions.
Independent_Variables: baseline condition (B1 vs B3);resource-pressure condition;inference configuration
Evaluation_Method: Paired McNemar; paired bootstrap CI of M(B1)-M(B3); E1;E2
Falsification_Condition: CI of degradation includes zero or lies within SESOI (equivalence)

Statement: Confidence-aware downstream verification recovers a measurable portion of the performance degradation introduced by resource-driven downgrading.
Independent_Variables: verification enabled (B5 vs B3);verification action;confidence threshold;resource-pressure condition
Evaluation_Method: Paired McNemar; bootstrap CI of recovery proportion; E2;E3
Falsification_Condition: CI of M(B5)-M(B3) includes zero or lies within SESOI at minimum coverage

Statement: Confidence-aware verification introduces measurable latency, energy, memory, or thermal overhead.
Evaluation_Method: Mixed-effects model or Wilcoxon signed-rank across runs; bootstrap CI; E1;E2
Falsification_Condition: No cost metric differs beyond measurement resolution

Statement: Confidence distributions and calibration characteristics differ between inference configurations operating under different resource conditions.
Evaluation_Method: Bootstrap CI of ECE/Brier differences; KS tests with Holm correction; E1

Statement: A joint resource-adaptation + confidence-verification policy provides a more favorable accuracy-efficiency trade-off than either mechanism alone.
Evaluation_Method: Pareto dominance and matched-budget comparison with bootstrap uncertainty; E2
Falsification_Condition: B5 dominated by or equivalent to B3 or B4; or B5 needs at least B1 cost

Statement: Resource adaptation produces no meaningful resource benefit.
Evaluation_Method: TOST on cost difference; E2
Falsification_Condition: Resource adaptation produces no meaningful resource benefit.

Statement: Confidence verification does not recover measurable performance.
Evaluation_Method: Paired McNemar; bootstrap CI; E2
Falsification_Condition: Confidence verification does not recover measurable performance.

Statement: Recovery is no better than simply using the static best model.
Evaluation_Method: Matched-cost comparison; Pareto dominance; E2
Falsification_Condition: Recovery is no better than simply using the static best model.

Statement: Verification overhead eliminates the efficiency benefit.
Evaluation_Method: Bootstrap CI on cost differences; E2
Falsification_Condition: Verification overhead eliminates the efficiency benefit.

Statement: Confidence calibration does not meaningfully change across configurations/resource states.
Evaluation_Method: Bootstrap CI; equivalence test; E1
Falsification_Condition: Confidence calibration does not meaningfully change across configurations/resource states.

Statement: The combined method does not outperform appropriate ablations.
Evaluation_Method: Pareto and matched-budget comparison; E2
Falsification_Condition: The combined method does not outperform appropriate ablations.

Statement: Forced-configuration sweep: C1-C4 under induced R0-R3, verification disabled.
Evaluation_Method: Per-cell accuracy, calibration and cost with repeated runs

Statement: Policy-driven episodes: B1-B5 under identical scripted resource-pressure schedules on identical item sequences.
Evaluation_Method: Paired item-level and run-level comparisons

Statement: Verification-policy ablation: B5 vs B5-F under the E2 schedules.
Independent_Variables: verification policy (configuration-aware vs fixed global threshold)
Evaluation_Method: Matched-rate and matched-cost comparison (H2.b)
